summary: Usage Insights totals in Console do not match invoice totals for selected time range
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports that Console → Usage Insights → Route/Model breakdown total for Feb 1–Feb 5 does not match the invoice usage total for the same period.
- Console shows: $18,742.61
- Invoice usage total shows: $19,008.14
- Delta: $265.53 (~1.40%)

Impact
- Finance team cannot use Usage Insights exports for internal chargeback/QBR because totals don’t reconcile with billing.
- Customer is on beta allowlist for Usage Insights and is using CSV export.

Customer expectation
- Totals should match invoice within small tolerance (customer asked for “exact” match, OK with documented rounding rules).

Environment
- Workspace: heliochat-prod
- Deployment mode: Hosted API
- Region: us-east
- Routes observed: /v1/chat/completions (majority), /v1/embeddings
- Models observed: llama-3.1-70b, llama-3.1-8b (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) In Console → Usage → Usage Insights
2) Time range: 2026-02-01 00:00 UTC → 2026-02-05 23:59 UTC
3) Group by Route + Model
4) Export CSV
5) Compare total_cost_usd sum to invoice line items for same workspace/time range

Notes
- Customer says the delta is not constant across days; some days match within ~$20, others are off by ~$80.
- Customer’s finance team is using UTC for invoice reconciliation.

Requested outcome
- Identify root cause and fix reconciliation for Usage Insights totals vs Billing totals.
- Provide customer-facing explanation and workaround until fix is deployed.
comments:
2026-02-06 09:18 (Dev Patel - Support)
Acknowledged. Looping in Cost Attribution + Console Backend. We’ll validate whether this is (a) rounding/timing boundary (b) credits/discount application (c) missing/late metering events or (d) double-counting retries/fallbacks.

Created internal tracking in ENG-3817 (reconciliation) and flagged as P1 due to finance workflow impact.

2026-02-06 10:02 (Markus Klein - Solutions Engineering)
From HelioChat: they’re reconciling against invoice usage subtotal excluding taxes/credits. They are not expecting committed-use discounts to be reflected in the Insights beta (they just want pre-discount usage to match invoice usage lines). They specifically called out /v1/chat/completions showing higher cost in invoice than in Console.

2026-02-06 11:11 (Nadia Rahman - Cost Attribution)
Initial hypothesis: Insights dataset uses request_start_time bucketed by hour; billing uses request_end_time (or ingestion time) for period boundaries. For multi-minute streaming sessions around midnight UTC, period assignment can differ. This would show up as day-to-day mismatch but should net out over longer ranges.

Action: pull sample of mismatched request_ids near boundary and confirm event_time semantics used by insights aggregation job.

2026-02-06 13:40 (Chloe Martin - Console Backend)
Checked query-service: breakdown endpoint sums cost_usd_attributed from analytics aggregate. That aggregate currently stores cost rounded to 4 decimals at hourly partition then re-summed. Billing line items store unrounded cost at request granularity and round at final invoice rendering.

If high volume, rounding-at-partition can create ~0.5–1.5% drift depending on distribution. Need to change to store integer microdollars (or store unrounded decimal) and round only at presentation.

2026-02-07 08:25 (Cole Summers - Billing)
Confirmed invoice usage subtotal is derived from metering event field billable_cost_microusd summed at request granularity, then rounded to cents at invoice generation. No discounts/credits in the number the customer quoted.

Also note: invoice includes retry attempts that were actually executed (each attempt generates a metering event). It does not include gateway-level “logical request retries” that never reached runtime.

2026-02-07 10:03 (Nadia Rahman - Cost Attribution)
Found two contributing factors:
1) Rounding drift: insights aggregate stores cost_usd as FLOAT with rounding at 4 decimals during rollup. Summing across many groups creates systematic undercount relative to micro-USD integer used for billing.
2) Late events: for us-east, ~0.2% of metering events arrive >2 hours late (mostly streaming disconnect + retry). Insights job for the current beta range was materializing hourly partitions with a 90-minute watermark; invoice uses full set (no watermark at generation time).

Net effect aligns with observed undercount in Insights vs invoice (~1.4%).

2026-02-07 10:41 (Dev Patel - Support)
Update drafted for customer:
- We identified a known beta limitation: rounding + late-arriving events can cause Usage Insights to undercount vs invoice for recent ranges.
- We’re implementing a fix to use integer micro-USD at aggregation and extending late-event handling.

Asked Eng for ETA and any recommended workaround for finance until fix ships.

2026-02-08 14:12 (Thomas Baird - Telemetry)
Proposed fix:
- Change aggregate schema to store cost_microusd (INT64) and tokens_in/out (INT64).
- Recompute last 14 days nightly (incremental backfill) until watermark extended and late events handled.
- Increase watermark from 90 minutes → 6 hours for beta, plus add a “data freshness / may be incomplete” banner.

Perf impact: minimal if we keep partitions hourly and only backfill recent partitions.

This aligns with ENG-3812/3817 work; we can land behind feature flag for Insights.

2026-02-10 09:30 (Chloe Martin - Console Backend)
Implemented server-side change to prefer cost_microusd when available and only round in API response. Added freshness metadata + banner support (ties into pr-23170).

Nadia/Cole: please confirm the reconciliation tolerance we should communicate during beta (e.g., <=0.1% once backfill completes).

2026-02-11 16:05 (Cole Summers - Billing)
After patch on staging with backfilled partitions, reconciliation vs billing export is within 0.03% for sample workspaces. Remaining delta is explainable by period boundary semantics for long-running streams, but that nets out if customer uses invoice period boundaries (UTC) and pulls completed partitions.

Recommendation: customer should avoid comparing “last 24 hours” until watermark/backfill finishes; for prior days it should reconcile.

2026-02-12 10:22 (Dev Patel - Support)
Sent customer update:
- Root cause confirmed: (1) rounding at aggregation time, (2) late-arriving metering events in streaming/retry scenarios.
- Fix scheduled and rolling out to prod behind beta flag; we’ll backfill recent days.
- Interim workaround: for reconciliation, use ranges ending at least 6 hours prior to “now” (reduces late-event impact) and prefer invoice’s UTC boundaries.

Customer asked for confirmation that exports will match invoice after fix and whether there will be an audit note in release notes.

2026-02-13 15:18 (Nadia Rahman - Cost Attribution)
Prod rollout complete for Insights allowlisted accounts in us-east. Backfill job completed for 2026-02-01 → 2026-02-12.

Re-ran HelioChat numbers:
- Console total now: $19,007.96
- Invoice usage total: $19,008.14
- Delta: $0.18 (0.001%)

This is within cent-level rounding variance.

Follow-up: we should document “freshness window” and show last_updated_at in UI (already in pr-23170).

2026-02-14 09:05 (Dev Patel - Support)
Confirmed with customer that totals now reconcile within rounding tolerance; customer validated on their side for the same range.

Resolution
- Adjusted insights aggregation to store and sum cost in micro-USD (integer) and only round at presentation/export.
- Extended late-event handling (watermark) and added freshness indicators to reduce comparisons against incomplete partitions.

Closing ticket. Linked to ongoing reconciliation hardening work in ENG-3817.
resolution: Fixed in beta rollout: cost aggregation now uses integer micro-USD (billing-consistent) + improved late-event handling and freshness indicators. Backfilled recent partitions; HelioChat totals reconcile within rounding tolerance.
